items.raw_excerpt: Thousands of elderly people are caring for loved ones well into their own 80s and 90s—with many unaware of the support available to them.

items.raw_excerpt: The ban on the use of smartphones in schools is to be extended to pupils in 7th and 9th grade as early as the next academic year, according to an amendment to the Pupils’ Statute due to be approved by the Council of Ministers.

items.raw_excerpt: Feeling slow and sluggish in these hot late summer days? You're not alone – and we have the perfect German word for you.
items.summary_en: The German word 'Hundstage' describes the hot and sluggish late summer days. Many people feel slow and tired during this time. This word captures the lazy summer feeling perfectly.

items.raw_excerpt: Police report catching fewer drink-drivers than during last summer's surveillance effort, even though they carried out 17 percent more breathalyser tests this year.
items.summary_en: Finnish police caught fewer drink-drivers this summer compared to last year, even though they performed 17 percent more breathalyser tests. However, they caught more drunk e-scooter riders than before.

items.raw_excerpt: There will be no continuation of the extended serving permit for alcohol that was introduced during the World Cup, Stockholm City Council voted yesterday.
items.summary_en: Stockholm City Council voted against continuing the extended alcohol serving hours. The extended permit was introduced during the World Cup. Bars and restaurants must now return to normal closing times.

items.raw_excerpt: A French student was fined 600 Singapore dollars (US$465) after pleading guilty Thursday to a public nuisance charge in Singapore for filming himself licking a straw from an orange juice vending machine and putting it back in what lawyers described as a social media stunt.
items.summary_en: A French student in Singapore pleaded guilty to public nuisance for licking a straw from an orange juice vending machine and putting it back. He was fined 600 Singapore dollars. Lawyers described the act as a social media stunt.

items.raw_excerpt: Iceland lags behind its Nordic neighbours in sign language interpretation and video interpreting services for Deaf people, according to the chair of the Icelandic Association of the Deaf, as hundreds gather in Selfoss for a major Nordic cultural festival. The four-yearly Nordic Deaf culture festival is being held in Iceland for the first time since…
items.summary_en: The Nordic Deaf culture festival is being held in Iceland for the first time. The chair of the Icelandic Association of the Deaf says Iceland lags behind its Nordic neighbors in sign language interpretation and video interpreting services. Hundreds gathered in Selfoss for the four-yearly cultural event.

items.raw_excerpt: This property-related phrase has a surprising military history.
items.summary_en: The French expression 'pied-a-terre' originally comes from military history, not real estate. Soldiers first used it to describe a temporary foothold during campaigns. Today it means a small secondary home in the city.

items.raw_excerpt: The lawn patterns were created when the garden was remodelled in the early 1800s.
items.summary_en: Hot weather has revealed the outline of a 19th-century parterre garden at Hardwick Hall in Derbyshire. The lawn patterns were created when the garden was remodelled in the early 1800s. A National Trust archaeologist says the parch marks are now more prominent than ever before.

items.raw_excerpt: The Thunder Bay International Airport is getting a hotel, marking the first Cambria Hotel to be built in Canada.
